assessments.reasoning: The questionnaire allows distinguishing de jure vs. de facto female headship because Section 1 records marital status in Question 6 ('Casado (a)', 'Separado (a)', 'Divorciado (a)', 'Viudo (a)', 'Unión Libre', 'Soltero (a)') alongside relationship to head in Question 3, and Section 3 captures remittances received from family abroad in Question 74, enabling identification of married/cohabiting women whose partners are absent from the roster. Women-maintained households can be identified through the main provider regardless of reference person because Section 3 records comprehensive individual income sources for every member aged 5 and older by line number. Conversely, unpartnered mother-child units cannot be uniquely identified within larger extended households because Question 3 only links members to the household head and lacks mother/parent line-number pointer variables. Finally, the instrument cannot link mother-child units to their own activity/consumption because household characteristics and consumption in Section 5 are recorded solely at the aggregate household level.
